items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Arben' only as a note marker; the interviewee (Vic Dickenson) narrates a story about meeting a 'raggedy' guy with Stump Brady, but does not explicitly name or describe a personal relationship with Arben.

ctx.x: Oh yeah! I was with Zack Whyte's band, and we went to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. And we were at some hotel there, some third-class hotel or fourth-class hotel or something... You know, we didn't have no money hardly, just scuffling, you know. And here comes this guy, and he was real raggedy, you know. We had a trombone player named Stump Brady. Stump, incidentally, was one of the best lead trombone players. He was really great, and I hope he still can play...

Anyhow, he brought this guy around to the room. And they had one of those Auburn(?) books. It's a big thing. It's a book that you learn in, but it's got all the...all of the trombone things, all the exercises and things that a trombone does.
